title: Heroic Ballad of Tirot Sing (Ka Sur Tirot Sing)
khasi_title: Ka Sur Tirot Sing Syiem Nongkhlaw
cultural_context: Ballad commemorating U Tirot Sing, ruler of Nongkhlaw, who led the Khasi resistance against the British East India Company from 1829 to 1833. Celebrated annually on July 17.
lyrics_khasi:
U Syiem ba shlur jong ka Ri Khasi,
Uba la ïeng pyrshah ïa ka bor nongwei,
Kham bha ban ïap kum u ksew ba laitluid,
Ban ïa kaba im kum u syiem ba mraw!

Ha ki riat ba rben ha ki lum ba jngai,
U la siat da u khnam, u la dung da ka wait;
Ka snam jong u ka la jaw ha ka khyndew,
Ban pynlong ia ka Ri ba kan laitluid man ka sngi!
lyrics_english:
The fearless Syiem of the Khasi motherland,
Who rose unbending against foreign conquerors,
Far better to perish as a free mountain warrior,
Than to live as a crowned and shackled slave!

Through steep ravines and deep mountain gorges,
He struck with the arrow, he slashed with the sword;
His royal blood poured out upon the sacred soil,
That our Motherland might stand free for all generations!

stanzas.title: Ka Ktien u Syiem (The Syiem's Declaration of Liberty)
stanzas.khasi:

stanzas.english: The fearless ruler who defied foreign conquest: Far better to die free than live as a chained slave!
